manifest.title: Ethora
manifest.author: Dappros Ltd
manifest.tagline: Your own chat server with a web app, admin panel and SDKs
manifest.description:
Ethora is a chat and messaging platform you run yourself: a web chat and
admin panel, an API, an XMPP server (ejabberd) and file storage, with mobile
and web SDKs on top. Create apps, users and chat rooms, and connect your own
clients through the API and the SDKs.

### Features

* Web chat and admin panel for apps, users, rooms and settings
* REST API (documented at `/api-docs/`) and real-time messaging over XMPP
* File sharing, stored in the app's own MinIO
* Multi-tenant: one server hosts many apps, each with its own users
* Web chat component and backend SDKs, and an MCP server for AI tools

### Licence

This is Ethora Core: free, with per-server limits of 5 apps and 500 user
accounts, raised to 10 and 5,000 by registering for free on the License page
of the admin panel. Licence: https://ethora.com/legal/ethora-core-license/
manifest.changelog: * First package: Ethora Core 2610.10 (API, web app, ejabberd, Centrifugo, MinIO)
manifest.postInstallMessage:
This app sets up its own administrator account on first start. The email is
`admin@` followed by the app's domain; the password is generated. To read
it, open the app's Web Terminal and run:

```
grep ADMIN_PASSWORD /app/data/secrets/secrets.env
```

Sign in at the app's address, then change the password in your account settings.
The XMPP server is reached over WebSocket at `/ws` on the same address; the
API lives under `/v1` and `/v2`.
